title: GfK/NIQ UK Consumer Confidence Barometer — October 2026: the first edition whose fieldwork covers the September policy week, and the last one before the Budget
source: EST: nielseniq.com/global/en/news-center/2026/headline-score-up-three-points-to-14-in-august/, fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200) — the August-2026 barometer release lists the remaining 2026 press-release dates verbatim as 'September 25th, October 23rd, November 20th and December 18th'. Corroborated the same session by a second, independently-published NIQ copy of the same list in the July-2026 release (news-center/2026/consumer-confidence-up-six-points-to-17-in-july/, fetched direct 2026-09-15: 'August 21, September 25, October 23, November 20, December 18'), whose August 21 entry has since matched the August edition's actual publication date. As with the September edition, the date is the FOURTH Friday, not the third the publisher's landing page gives as its rule of thumb ('the third Friday of the month in most months, with a publication schedule available at the start of the year', fetched direct 2026-09-15) — the dated list is the key, the convention is not. Release time not verifiable from any NIQ primary this session. Filed estimate on the standard three counts: this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for GfK/NIQ, and the schedule is a note inside a press release. Discovered in the adjacency sweep of the never-assessed initial research of uk-consumer-confidence-2026-09-25, 2026-09-15
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-consumer-confidence-2026-09-25 LANE, 2026-09-15, in the same PR that wrote that event's canonical file. It earns its own slot for a reason the proposer's research made mechanical rather than decorative: the September edition's fieldwork CLOSES BEFORE the September policy week (every September window in the three-year primary sample ended on or before the 13th — 2023: Sep 1-13; 2024: Aug 30-Sep 13; 2025: Sep 1-11), so fomc-2026-09-16, uk-cpi-2026-09-16 and boe-decision-2026-09-17 cannot be in it. THIS edition is the one that carries them: an October window running roughly 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-09 on the same pattern. It is also the LAST barometer before uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28, which puts its fieldwork at the peak of pre-Budget tax-rise speculation — the configuration that produced the two negative Septembers in the series (2024, Budget 10-30, -7 points; 2025, Budget 11-26, -2 points with NIQ's own commentary naming anticipated tax rises). In 2024 the chill persisted into October (-21 after -20) and reversed only after the Budget resolved. SAME-DAY PAIRING ALREADY ON THE CALENDAR: uk-retail-sales-2026-10-23 publishes the same morning, which makes 2026-10-23 the single date carrying both halves of the survey-versus-till disagreement this lane is tracking. Expected LOW on the same measured grounds as every UK sibling: symbols [], no UK-listed name in this book, no sterling- or rates-keyed house playbook. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
